protocol.title: Digital Microfluidics for Automated Proteomic Processing
protocol.sample: Serum proteins / bovine serum albumin (BSA) as model protein
protocol.objective: Fully automated, integrated proteomic sample processing on a DMF device: protein extraction by precipitation, resolubilization, reduction, alkylation, and tryptic digestion, followed by nano-HPLC-MS/MS identification

bottom_plate.hydrophobic_layer: Teflon-AF, 50 nm (1% wt/wt in Fluorinert FC-40, spin-coated at 2000 rpm, 60 s)

device.gap: 140 um (set by double-sided tape, two pieces)

actuation.control_hardware: Home-built control box with high-voltage relays (NI DaqPad), function generator, amplifier

device.electrode_dimensions: 1 mm square, 50 um gaps; 2.5 mm square reservoirs

working_buffer.name: WB
working_buffer.composition: 100 mM TrisHCl pH 7.8, 0.08% Pluronic F127 w/v
working_buffer.notes: Pluronic F127 surfactant prevents biofouling on device surface

precipitant.name: TCA
precipitant.notes: Denatures and precipitates proteins by pH drop and hydration shell disruption

waste_reservoir.name: R-3
waste_reservoir.notes: Receives supernatant after precipitation and wash eluates

wash_buffer.name: WashBuffer
wash_buffer.notes: Removes residual TCA and non-protein contaminants from precipitate

resolubilizing_buffer.name: AmBic buffer
resolubilizing_buffer.composition: 100 mM Ammonium Bicarbonate pH 8.0, 0.08% Pluronic F127 w/v
resolubilizing_buffer.notes: Redissolves protein precipitate after drying; compatible with trypsin digestion

alkylating_agent.name: IAM
alkylating_agent.notes: Alkylates free thiols to prevent re-oxidation; incubation protected from light

sub_steps.action: Prepare working buffer (WB): 100 mM TrisHCl pH 7.8, 0.08% Pluronic F127 w/v
Dissolve protein(s) in WB; pipette into R-1 on device
Prepare 20% TCA in DI water; pipette into R-2
Prepare 70/30 Chloroform/ACN wash buffer; pipette into R-4
Prepare 100 mM AmBic pH 8.0, 0.08% Pluronic F127 resolubilizing buffer; pipette into R-5
Dissolve TCEP at 10 mM in WB; pipette into R-6
Dissolve IAM at 12 mM in WB; pipette into R-7
Dissolve trypsin in WB at 1/5 of total protein concentration; pipette into R-8

steps.name: Protein Extraction by Precipitation
steps.notes: Protein droplet (R-1) and TCA precipitant droplet (R-2) merged. Combined droplet incubates 5 min; proteins precipitate onto device surface. Supernatant actuated to waste reservoir R-3 (Figure 2, Frame 4).

steps.name: Precipitate Washing
steps.operation: dispense + drive across precipitate + drain to R-3
steps.notes: Three sequential wash buffer droplets dispensed from R-4 and driven across precipitated protein to waste R-3. Removes residual TCA and non-protein contaminants. Modelled in BioScript as 3 unrolled dispense/drain pairs (no loop construct in compiler).

steps.name: Protein Resolubilization
steps.operation: allow precipitate to dry + dispense buffer + incubate
steps.notes: Precipitate allowed to dry on surface. Resolubilizing buffer (AmBic + Pluronic) dispensed from R-5 and incubated 20 min until precipitate fully dissolves. In BioScript, a second ProteinSample dispense abstracts the on-surface precipitate re-contacted with buffer.

steps.name: Reduction
steps.notes: TCEP droplet (R-6) merged with sample. Mixed in circular 6-electrode pattern. Incubated 1 h at room temperature in humidified chamber to reduce disulfide bonds.

steps.name: Alkylation
steps.operation: dispense + merge + circular mix (6-electrode) + incubate in dark
steps.mixing_pattern: Circular actuation across 6 electrodes (same as reduction)
steps.notes: IAM droplet (R-7) merged with reduced sample. Mixed as in S5. Incubated 15 min at room temperature protected from light to alkylate free thiols.

steps.name: Tryptic Digestion
steps.operation: dispense + merge + circular mix (6-electrode) + incubate on hot plate
steps.mixing_pattern: Circular actuation across 6 electrodes (same as reduction)
steps.notes: Trypsin droplet (R-8) merged with alkylated sample. Mixed as in S5. Incubated 3 h at 37 C on hot plate in humidified chamber. Trypsin cleaves at Lys-X and Arg-X.

steps.name: Post-Processing Sample Preparation (off-chip)

sub_steps.action: Remove top substrate; quench digestion by adding 0.6 mL of 2.5% trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) in water
Purify quenched product using C18 ZipTips (Millipore, Billerica, MA) per manufacturer instructions
Dilute purified sample in DI water to a final volume of 100 mL

steps.notes: Off-chip post-processing. TFA quenches trypsin activity. C18 ZipTip SPE desalts and concentrates peptides.

instrument.trap_column: 3 mm dia. C18 beads, 150 um ID x 2.5 cm
instrument.separation_column: 3 um dia. C18 beads, 75 um ID x 15 cm (reversed-phase)
instrument.emitter: Nanoelectrospray emitter, 20 um ID tapered to 10 um ID (NewObjective)

lc_method.loading: 2 uL sample at 5 uL/min in 5% acetonitrile in water onto trap column

database_search.software: SEQUEST (incorporated in Bioworks v3.01, Thermo-Fisher Scientific)

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.description: Precipitation, washing, resolubilization, reduction, alkylation, digestion, QC detect

cfg.shape: Diamond (single conditional split, two branches, one join/terminal)

bioscript_compiler_notes.ir_output: 4 basic blocks (BB1-BB4), 1 if/else gate, 4 CFG edges
bioscript_compiler_notes.duration_units: All durations in minutes (m) or seconds (s); BioScript supports s and m only

abstraction_notes.precipitation: mix + drain abstracts TCA-driven protein precipitation and supernatant removal to R-3; no native precipitate primitive in BioScript
abstraction_notes.wash_unrolling: 3 wash steps unrolled as explicit dispense/drain pairs; no loop construct in lilott8/BioScript compiler
abstraction_notes.resolubilization: second ProteinSample dispense abstracts on-surface dried precipitate being re-contacted with buffer droplet
abstraction_notes.circular_mixing: BioScript mix abstracts both the circular 6-electrode actuation and the subsequent timed incubation
abstraction_notes.temperature: heat at 25c models room-temperature incubation; heat at 37c models hot plate for trypsin digestion
abstraction_notes.drain_vs_dispose: drain used for waste/failed paths; dispose used for successfully processed droplets at QC gate
